items.title: Top 5 Biggest Asteroids (#1 Is Also a Dwarf Planet) #shorts
items.description:
The five biggest asteroids, counted down from #5 to #1, each one drawn to the same scale.
Full video: What If an Asteroid Hit the Ocean? A 10 km Rock Would Hit the Seafloor

Sources
• NASA / JPL (Dawn mission): Ceres is 939.4 km across, the largest object in the asteroid belt, recognized as a dwarf planet, holds about 25% of the belt's mass; its bright spots in Occator crater are salt (sodium carbonate) deposits
• NASA / JPL (Dawn mission): Vesta has a mean diameter of 525.4 km; the central peak of its Rheasilvia basin is about 22 km high
• Marsset et al. 2020 (Nature Astronomy): Pallas is about 511 km across; its orbit is inclined about 35° to the plane of the planets; no spacecraft has visited it
• Vernazza et al. 2019 (ESO VLT/SPHERE, Nature Astronomy): Hygiea is about 434 km across and nearly spherical — a candidate for the smallest dwarf planet
• Hanuš et al. 2020 (ESO VLT): Interamnia about 332 km across (older estimates 306–326 km); named after Teramo, Italy (Latin: Interamnia)
• Own calculations: time to drive around each one at 100 km/h = π × diameter / 100 (Interamnia ≈ 10 h, Ceres ≈ 30 h)

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.

items.title: If Earth Were a Basketball, the Space Station Would Fly 7 mm Above It #shorts
items.description:
Shrink Earth to a basketball: the edge of space is thinner than a coin, the space station flies 7.5 mm up, and the Moon is a tennis ball 7 m away.
Full video: What If the Moon Crashed Into Earth? You'd Have 4 Days

Sources
• NASA Earth Fact Sheet: Earth's mean diameter 12,742 km; Moon mean distance 384,400 km; Moon diameter 3,474.8 km
• NASA: the International Space Station orbits at about 400 km (roughly 250 miles) altitude
• Kármán line: the commonly used boundary of space at 100 km altitude (FAI)
• Size 7 basketball: about 75 cm circumference, 23.9 cm diameter
• Own calculations at 23.9 cm per 12,742 km: 100 km = 1.9 mm, 400 km = 7.5 mm, Moon distance = 7.2 m, Moon diameter = 6.5 cm (tennis ball ≈ 6.7 cm)

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#shorts #space #earth #scale

items.title: Squeeze Earth Into a Marble and It Becomes a Black Hole #shorts
items.description:
All of Earth's mass, squeezed to 1.77 cm: that is Earth's event horizon. The Sun would need to be just 5.9 km wide.
Full video: What Happens If You Fall Into a Black Hole?

Sources
• NASA Earth Fact Sheet: Earth's mass 5.972 × 10^24 kg, mean diameter 12,742 km; NASA Sun Fact Sheet: Sun's mass 1.989 × 10^30 kg
• Schwarzschild radius r = 2GM/c² (G = 6.674 × 10^-11, c = 299,792 km/s)
• Own calculations: Earth r = 8.87 mm (17.7 mm across, about a marble); Sun r = 2.95 km (5.9 km across, about 70 minutes on foot at 5 km/h); squeeze factor 12,742 km / 17.7 mm ≈ 720 million
• NASA: stellar-mass black holes form when massive stars collapse at the end of their lives

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#shorts #space #blackhole #physics
